story: ECB data on AI use at work in the euro area (ECB Blog, 27 Nov 2026)
method: Primary page fetched twice from this environment (09:59 and 10:04 UTC); canonical URL matches; publication time checked in the ECB Blog RSS feed; every script figure matched word for word to the post's text; Bloomberg's independent report returned HTTP 403 (paywall) and is recorded as secondary (headline via Techmeme feed); no correction, update or withdrawal notice on the page or in the RSS feed.

ecb_blog.host_owner: European Central Bank (ecb.europa.eu), canonical URL matches
ecb_blog.authors: Dimitris Georgarakos, Geoff Kenny, Justus Meyer (ECB Research)
ecb_blog.note: ECB Blog disclaimer: views are the authors' and not necessarily those of the ECB/Eurosystem; data from the ECB Consumer Expectations Survey

bloomberg.note: paywalled/blocked; headline read via Techmeme feed (https://www.techmeme.com/feed.xml, item 27 Nov 2026 13:15 EST)

claims.claim: The European Central Bank published new data on AI use at work on Friday 27 November 2026
evidence: ECB Blog post 'AI, jobs and prices: what euro area consumers expect': 'New evidence from the ECB's Consumer Expectations Survey sheds light on consumers' views on jobs, prices and AI regulation.'
claims.contradictions: It is a blog post by ECB economists (views not necessarily the ECB's); the script says 'new data from the European Central Bank', which is accurate: the data is the ECB's own survey.

claims.claim: In August 2026, 44% of employed euro area consumers used AI at least weekly at work; around 18% daily
evidence: 'In August 2026, 44% of employed euro area consumers reported using AI at least weekly at work, and around 18% used it daily.'
claims.contradictions: One aggregator (emergent.sh, search excerpt) says 40%; the primary says 44%, and Bloomberg's headline says 44%. Primary wins.
claims.decision: USE ('nearly half', '44 percent', 'about 18 percent'; scope: working people in the euro area)

claims.claim: Around 56% of workplace AI users say AI increases the amount of work they complete
evidence: 'Around 56% say that AI increases the amount of work they complete, while 47% report producing higher-quality output.'
claims.contradictions: This figure is from the June 2026 wave (chart notes), not August; the script does not date it.

claims.claim: Among users with no increase in output, the most cited reason is the time needed to check or correct AI-generated results
evidence: 'Among users who reported no increase in output, the most commonly cited reason is the time needed to check or correct AI-generated results (Chart 2, panel b).'
claims.decision: USE (script: 'the top reason was the time spent checking and fixing the AI's work')

claims.claim: Euro area workers use AI daily more than US workers
evidence: 'a larger share of consumers in the euro area report using AI daily' but notes say CES and Gallup use different questions and samples, so comparisons are indicative

corrections: Draft said 'workers in Europe'; corrected to 'eurozone' / 'euro area' (11 countries covered by the survey).
excluded: EU vs US comparison (surveys not harmonised)
